PRODUCT GUIDE

The Quintara app and web app, screen by screen

What members, guests and staff see and do across the mobile app, the web app and the admin console, with an honest account of what is built and what is still a mock-up.

6 October 2026Screens shown are from the clickable mock-upNames, venues and prices are placeholders

01Overview

Quintara is a private membership for founders, creators, investors and hosts, starting in Cape Town. One account opens three surfaces that share the same data.

Mobile appThe member's everyday companion: invitations, bookings, tickets, the concierge and QÉRA, built for one hand.
Web appThe same membership on a larger canvas, and the public face where guests discover Quintara and apply.
Admin consoleWhere Quintara staff review applications, run experiences, answer requests and keep content current.

Three ideas shape every screen:

  • Curated, not endless. Home is a short, chosen page. There is no feed to scroll.
  • Controlled introductions. Contact details stay private. Introductions and opportunities pass through the Quintara team with consent on both sides.
  • Run by staff, not developers. Experiences, tiers, partners, privileges and announcements are edited in the admin console.

02Who uses it

PERSONWHAT THEY CAN DO
GuestBrowse experiences open to guests, Lifestyle partners, Quintara TV and the Boutique; apply for membership. Member areas show a lock with a path to apply or sign in.
MemberEverything a guest can, plus booking at member prices, the member directory and messaging, the concierge, privileges, opportunities, QÉRA and a digital membership card.
Founder, investor, creatorAdditions to membership, not separate accounts. Investor access is switched on by staff after verification and is never granted by applying.
Concierge deskRuns experiences and guest lists, checks guests in, and answers member requests. Cannot decide memberships.
AdministratorEverything the desk can, plus applications, members, tiers, payments, partners and content.

03The mobile app

Five tabs along the bottom. QÉRA sits raised in the centre as the signature action; everything else in the membership is one tap behind More.

HomeInvitation, quick actions, next booking, suggestions
ExperiencesThe calendar, filters, booking and tickets
QÉRAAsk, plan and confirm
ClubDirectory, introductions, profiles
MoreConcierge, Lifestyle, Privileges, Opportunities, Quintara TV, Boutique, Bookings, Messages, Profile

Search, messages and notifications live in the header of every main screen. Inner screens have a back chevron and a centred title.

Arriving and joining

The application takes four short steps (about you, your work, why Quintara, review). The applicant then follows its status: submitted, under review, interview if needed, approved, payment, active.

Home and experiences

How booking behaves depends on the experience: open and members-only experiences confirm at once while seats remain; full ones offer the waitlist; some ask for an application; and invitation-only experiences show no booking button until staff invite the member.

05The admin console

The staff side works on the same data as the member apps, so a decision made here appears to the member straight away.

Other screens in the console: Members (suspend and reinstate), Tiers (names and fees), Concierge desk (reply and move requests through their stages), Partners and privileges, Orders, Content (the home announcement) and Photography.

06How it fits together

From guest to member

  1. A guest applies in the app or on the web. The draft is saved as they go.
  2. Staff start the review in the admin console, and invite the applicant to a conversation if needed.
  3. Staff choose a tier and approve. The applicant sees the offer and the fee.
  4. The applicant pays. The membership activates with a number, a card and member access.

From invitation to the door

  1. Staff publish an experience and invite members, or leave it open to book.
  2. The member reserves. If it is full they join the waitlist; staff release seats and confirm.
  3. A ticket with a code appears in the app, and a notification confirms it.
  4. At the door, staff check the guest in from the guest list or by code.

From request to done

  1. The member writes to the concierge, or confirms a plan QÉRA has drafted.
  2. The desk reviews and replies with options inside the request.
  3. The member confirms an option; the desk books it and marks the request complete.

07What exists today

Two things exist side by side: a clickable mock-up that shows the whole product, and production code that so far covers its first slice.

The mock-up runs in a browser on sample data and remembers what you do in that browser only. The production code has a real server and database, a web app, a staff app and automated tests, and still needs hosting, a sign-in provider and a payment provider before real members can use it.

FEATURECLICKABLE MOCK-UPPRODUCTION CODE

Sign-inSimulatedDevelopment stand-in; identity provider not connected

Tiers, payments ledger, content, photography (staff)WorkingNo staff screens yet

The mock-up and the production code are separate. Changing one does not change the other; the mock-up is the reference for what the production build should become.

08Design language

PaletteNear-black ground, ivory type, soft stone hairlines, and champagne used sparingly for the current page, invitations and the QÉRA button.
TypographyCormorant Garamond for titles, often in italic, echoing the logo's serif. Jost for everything functional.
LogoThe emblem and wordmark appear on the welcome screen, in each header and sidebar, on the membership card, and as a quiet watermark where photography will sit.
PhotographyNone is in place yet. Staff can add a photograph to any experience, partner or product from the admin console's Photography screen.

09What comes next

  1. Decisions only you can make: real membership tiers and fees, the launch calendar of experiences, the first partners and privileges, and photography.
  2. Providers to choose: hosting, a sign-in provider, and a South African payment provider that supports recurring membership fees.
  3. Production build, in order: connect the mobile app to the server; payment for experiences and refunds; live message delivery; then QÉRA on real data.
  4. Before launch: an independent security test and a privacy review against POPIA.
